page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-2 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the n2 family. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.8 GHz, configured as 1 physical core with 2 threads. The instance is equipped with 2.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and has zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks position this instance in the lower tiers. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance score is 1399.29, while the multi-core score is 1841.88. Memory bandwidth tests show read-only large block speeds of 13.72 GB/sec and write speeds of 11.78 GB/sec. Geekbench scores reflect similar constraints, with a single-core score of 1111.0 and a multi-core score of 1311.0. The CPU supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and AES cryptography, which assist in specific mathematical and encryption workloads despite the overall low resource footprint.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the n2-highcpu-2 offers a low-cost entry point for workloads requiring dedicated CPU allocation rather than shared-core burstable resources. However, the low memory density of 1 GB per vCPU represents a significant tradeoff for memory-intensive applications. This server is best suited for lightweight compute-bound tasks, basic static web serving, simple command-line utilities, or small CI/CD build agents that do not require substantial memory or local storage.
